chunks: One who was temperate among them, said: "Did I not say to you: 'Why don't you praise God?'"

key_terms.أَوْسَطُهُمْ: The most moderate/balanced one among them

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the moderate one's reminder to praise God in this narration?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this narration is often linked to the concept of *al-Wusta* (the middle way), illustrating how the moderate individual serves as a moral compass within the community by gently correcting collective negligence. It underscores the social responsibility of *Amr bil Ma'ruf* (enjoining good), where consistent remembrance of God (*Tasbih*) is not merely personal piety but a communal obligation to maintain spiritual equilibrium.
